entries.title: Strada della Mendola verso Bolzano e le Dolomiti, Amonn postcard M 10511: the German title covered, then the card printed again in Italian
text: The road over the Mendola pass, cut into the rock above the Adige valley, with a motor car on the bend and the Dolomites across the valley. Johann F. Amonn of Bozen published the view as card M 10511.

Two copies stand side by side. On the first, kept by the Palais Mamming Museum in Meran, the Italian title “Strada della Mendola verso Bolzano e le Dolomiti” is printed across the top of the picture, and the German title below it lies under a long black bar. The second is the same card printed again by the same publisher. Nothing is written on the front; the Italian title runs along the back, the imprint now reads “Joh. F. Amonn Bolzano”, and a line says “Riproduzione vietata”. The picture was retouched as well: the bank of cloud is gone from the sky and the mountains stand larger. This copy carries the stamp of the Hotel Caldaro on the Mendola and a handwritten date, 8 April 1930.
One copy was corrected by hand; the other was made new, with nothing left to correct. The covering on the first is not dated.
facts: Palais Mamming inv. 25651, imprint 'Joh. F. Amonn Bozen M 10511 n', 1904–1914: 'Strada della Mendola verso Bolzano e le Dolomiti (sekundäre italienische Beschriftung, die ursprünglich Deutsche wurde geschwärzt)' (record)
Second copy: heimatsammlung.de, image '4893-postkarte-mendel.jpg' (found by the author, 24 Nov 2026), front and back in one picture with the site's watermark (compare_18.04/findings.md)

Seen in the image (Mamming copy): the Mendola road cut into a rock face above the Adige valley, a car on the bend, a bank of cloud over low mountains; at the top the italic Italian title above a long black bar
Seen in the image (second copy, front): the same road, rock, wall, poles and car; no title; a clear blue sky with small clouds and the mountains larger and lit pink

Seen in the image (second copy, back): 'STRADA DELLA MENDOLA VERSO BOLZANO E LE DOLOMITI' printed upright along the dividing line under a tree mark; the oval 'Joh. F. Amonn Bolzano'; 'Riproduzione vietata.'; 'M 10511 n'; a violet stamp 'Hotel Caldaro / Propr. Herrnhofer / Mendola'; handwritten '8. 4. 30.'; no postage stamp or address

entries.title: Kurort Meran, Amonn postcard M 14509, before and after “in Süd-Tirol” was blacked out
text: The parish church of St. Nikolaus in Meran, seen from a path under a vine pergola, with a woman in a straw hat on the path. Johann F. Amonn of Bozen published the view as card M 14509 with the caption “Kurort Meran / in Süd-Tirol.”

Two copies of the card stand side by side. The first is the card as printed. On the second, kept by the Palais Mamming Museum in Meran, the words “in Süd-Tirol” lie under a black bar and “Merano. Chiesa parrocchiale” is printed above the old caption, across the woman's skirt. Only the lettering was changed: the picture, the woman included, is the same card. Her skirt is crimson on the first copy and grey on the second, where the red has faded or was printed weaker throughout.
The covering is not dated. The name Tirol was banned in August 1923 (row 16.06).
facts: Palais Mamming inv. 23354, 'Joh. F. Amonn Bozen M 14509 n': title 'Merano. Chiesa parocchiale Kurort Meran in Südtirol ("in Südtirol" geschwärzt)', dated 1904–1925 (record)
The ban on 'Tirol' and its derivatives took effect on 23 Aug 1923 according to the Touriseum (notes 18, §1, [V record])

Second copy: Aukro listing Z1409, 18 June 2025, https://aukro.cz/merano-meran-mesto-hory-sudtirol-alpy-italie-z1409-7017297764 ; unposted; back 'Joh. F. Amonn Bozen', 'M 14509', 'Kunstverlag Leo Stainer, Innsbruck.', 'JFA BOZEN' in the stamp box, '5013724' at the right edge (compare_18.05/findings.md)
Whether the 'n' of 'M 14509 n' in the Mamming record marks another printing is not known (compare_18.05/findings.md)

Seen in the image (Aukro copy): the caption 'Kurort Meran / in Süd-Tirol.' alone at lower left; the woman with a red band on her hat, a yellow striped blouse, a blue bundle under her arm and a crimson skirt

Seen in the image (Mamming copy): 'Merano. Chiesa parrocchiale' over 'Kurort Meran', a black bar over the line below; the woman in the same place and pose, her skirt grey-brown; the church roof grey-brown and the tower without red

entries.title: Meran, Romanisches Portal im Schloss Tirol, Bährendt postcard B 39: the German struck through, “Merano, Porta Romana” printed over
text: A Romanesque doorway in Schloss Tirol above Meran, its carved arch and the beasts on either side. Leo Bährendt of Meran photographed and published it as card B 39, with the caption “Meran, Romanisches Portal im Schloss Tirol” and on the back “Photographie und Verlag von Leo Bährendt, Meran”.

Two copies stand side by side, fronts above and backs below. The first is the card as printed. On the second, kept by the Palais Mamming Museum, a row of short bars is printed through the German caption and “Merano, Porta Romana” above it; on the back the publisher's line is printed over in Italian, “Fotografo e Editore Leo Baehrendt Merano”.
The Italian caption does not translate the German one. “Romanisches Portal”, a Romanesque doorway, becomes “Porta Romana”, a Roman gate.
facts: Palais Mamming inv. 9010, Leo Bährendt, Meran: 'Der deutsche Text "Meran - Romanisches Portal im Schloß Tirol" wurde durchgestrichen und durch den italienischen Text "Merano, Porta Romana" ersetzt. Auf der Rückseite wurde der deutsche Text "Photograph u. Verlag Leo Bährendt, Meran" ebenfalls durchgestrichen und durch "Fotografo e Editore Leo Baehrendt Merano" ersetzt', dated 1925–1943 (record)

First copy: a dealer's listing on oldthing, image https://img.oldthing.net/i/webp/9985/52/86/95/52869532_0_s.webp (found by the author, 24 Nov 2026), front and back served at 317 × 500 only (compare_18.16/findings.md)

Seen in the image (first copy, back): printed upright at the left edge 'Photographie und Verlag von Leo Bährendt, Meran. 1913. No. B. 39' (the year read on a small scan); a number in the stamp box, unreadable
Seen in the image (covered copy, front): 'Merano, Porta Romana' above a printed row of short vertical bars over a red German line

Seen in the image (covered copy, back): 'Fotografo e Editore Leo Baehrendt Merano No. B 39' printed upright at the left edge over traces of an earlier imprint; '280623' in the stamp box; museum pencil notes 'Inv. N° 9010'
The Italian turns 'Romanisches Portal' (Romanesque portal) into 'Porta Romana' (Roman gate) [INF] (notes 18, §2)
